items.text: Does the map contain a title?
items.explanation: The map title defines its purpose/topic, and possibly its spatial and temporal scope.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.2.1 – Název mapy, str. 58)

items.text: Does the map contain map credits?
items.explanation: Map credits provide information about the author/institution, data sources, publication date, licence and copyright.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.2.5 – Tiráž, str. 65)

items.text: Does the web map application have an accessible legend?
items.explanation: Is the legend visible in the default state of the application, or can it be easily found and displayed?
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.2.3 – Legenda, str. 61–64)

LONGLEY, Paul A. et al. Geographic Information Systems and Science. Wiley, 2011. (2011)

items.text: Is the legend consistent with cartographic rules?
items.explanation: A legend is a list of symbols shown in the map and their explanation.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.2.3 – Legenda, str. 61–64)

UCGIS GIS&T Body of Knowledge – Cartography and Visualization (CV)

subitems.text: Is the legend complete (everything shown in the map is included in the legend)?
Is the legend independent – does it show only one symbol for one phenomenon?
Is the legend properly organized – does thematic content take precedence over topographic content?
Is the legend consistent with the map symbols (everything in the legend is also present in the map)?

items.text: Is a map scale available?
items.explanation: Scale is essential for interpreting distances. It may be graphical, numerical or verbal.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.2.4 – Měřítko, str. 64)
MIKLÍN, Jan et al. Tvorba map. Ostrava: OU, 2018.

Metody tematické kartografie (Voženílek, V., Kaňok, J., a kol., 2011)
LONGLEY, Paul A. et al. Geographic Information Systems and Science. Wiley, 2011. (2011)

items.text: Does the scale change dynamically according to map position and zoom level?
items.explanation: This ensures that scale information remains up to date during user interaction with the map.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.
Kapitola 6.2.4 – Měřítko, str. 64)
KRAAK, Menno-Jan et al. Mapping for a Sustainable World. UN, 2020.
Section 4.3 Interactive Maps)

items.text: Is the map field the most dominant element?
items.explanation: Does the map field occupy at least 75% of the browser window in the default state of the application?
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.
Kapitola 6.4.3 – Vliv vizuální hierarchie, str. 79–80)
MIKLÍN, Jan et al. Tvorba map. Ostrava: OU, 2018.

KRAAK, Menno-Jan et al. Mapping for a Sustainable World. UN, 2020. (Kraak et al., 2020 – Section 2.13 Layout & Visual Hierarchy)
UCGIS GIS&T Body of Knowledge – Cartography and Visualization (CV)

items.text: Is proper visual hierarchy maintained in the map?
items.explanation: Visual hierarchy determines the order and prominence of map layers – order: 1) main thematic content, 2) supplementary thematic content, 3) topographic background.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.4.3 – Vliv vizuální hierarchie, str. 79–80)
MIKLÍN, Jan et al. Tvorba map. Ostrava: OU, 2018. (Miklín, Dušek, Krtička, Kaláb, 2018 – Kapitola 10.1 Základní principy vizuálního designu)
KRAAK, Menno-Jan et al. Mapping for a Sustainable World. UN, 2020. (Kraak et al., 2020 – Section 2.13 Layout & Visual Hierarchy)
UCGIS GIS&T Body of Knowledge – Cartography and Visualization (CV)

items.text: Do the thematic layers in the map follow cartographic conventions?
items.explanation: This includes appropriate use of symbols and colours, colour progression in scales, blue for water, and established symbol standards.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.
Kapitola 6.6.2 – Barva, str. 88–89

items.text: Is the map symbol key appropriately chosen and consistent with cartographic rules?
items.explanation: The choice of point, line and area symbols must be understandable. This also concerns cartographic semantics.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.
Kapitola 6.7 – Vybrané vyjadřovací metody, str. 96–118)

LONGLEY, Paul A. et al. Geographic Information Systems and Science. Wiley, 2011. (2011)

items.text: Are map elements appropriately generalized with respect to the zoom level?
items.explanation: Cartographic generalization is the selection, graphical simplification and abstraction of objects, phenomena and their relationships for their graphical representation in a map. It ensures that, at different zoom levels, the map does not display excessive or overly detailed elements that would reduce its readability and clarity.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.1.4 – Úroveň měřítka, str. 53–56)

items.text: Does the size or level of detail of symbols change depending on scale (zoom-dependent symbology)?
items.explanation: Adapting symbols to scale improves map readability when zooming in and out.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Is the cartographic projection implemented as Web Mercator?
items.explanation: Web Mercator is the most widely used projection in web cartography and ensures compatibility with common basemaps.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.1.1 – Kartografické zobrazení, str. 46–50)

items.text: Is the map responsive and does it adapt to the browser window size?
items.explanation: The map should remain usable when the browser window size changes or on different types of devices.
items.source:
NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.
Kapitola 7.5 – Optimalizace pro mobilní zařízení, str. 127–131)
KRAAK, Menno-Jan et al. Mapping for a Sustainable World. UN, 2020.
Section 4.6 Mobile Maps & Responsive Design)

items.text: Does the application allow switching thematic layers?
items.explanation: The user should have control over which data are currently displayed.

items.text: Does the application allow reading coordinates in [lat, lon] format?
items.explanation: Allows the user to obtain the exact position of a point.

items.text: Can the user switch between different basemaps?
items.explanation: The user can choose different contexts (orthophoto, topographic map, base map).

items.text: If map rotation is enabled, is there a north indicator and a reset orientation button?
items.explanation: When the map is rotated, the user must be able to determine orientation and reset it easily.

items.text: Are points automatically clustered when zooming out to prevent symbol overlap?
items.explanation: Clustering reduces symbol overlap and improves readability at smaller scales.

items.text: Is the selected thematic mapping method appropriate for the given data type?
items.explanation: The chosen cartographic method should correspond to the data type and map purpose.

items.text: Is the user informed that heatmaps are only indicative and not suitable for precise value reading?
items.explanation: Heatmaps are intended for general visualization of intensity, not precise data interpretation.

items.text: In dot maps, do dot size or value change dynamically with zoom level?
items.explanation: Dot maps should adapt to zoom level to maintain readability and interpretability.

items.text: Do point symbols use outlines, halos, or shadows to improve contrast against the background?
items.explanation: Additional visual enhancements improve symbol visibility against basemaps.

items.text: Are vector data optimized for web use (e.g. GeoJSON, TopoJSON)?
items.explanation: Optimized vector data reduce file size and improve rendering performance.

items.text: Are raster layers served using standardized tile services?
items.explanation: Tile services are an efficient standard for publishing raster data on the web.

items.text: Does the application use open and standardized data formats for interoperability?
items.explanation: Using open formats improves interoperability and data exchange.

items.text: Does the application allow zooming?
items.explanation: The ability to zoom in and out is a basic interaction for working with a web map.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.1.4 – Úroveň měřítka, str. 53–56)

items.text: Is the functionality of GIS tools clear (icon, label, tooltip)?
items.explanation: The controls should be understandable to the user.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.3.1 – Ovládací prvky, str. 67–69)

items.text: Do the map composition and controls follow GIS conventions and standards?
items.explanation: The application should follow common behaviour patterns known from GIS systems.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.3–6.4 – Ovládací prvky a celková kompozice mapy, str. 67–80)

items.text: Can the map be manipulated using a mouse?
items.explanation: Basic interactivity (panning, zooming) is essential for usability.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 2.8 – Interaktivita, dynamika, str. 21–27)

items.text: Is the application user interface (including all application elements) consistently in one language?
items.explanation: All parts of the application should be consistently in one language (e.g. only Czech or only English) to maintain maximum clarity.
items.source:
WORLD WIDE WEB CONSORTIUM (W3C). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG). (WCAG)
Frontend Web Performance Checklist

items.text: Is the font size in the application adjusted for easy readability?
items.explanation: Text elements should be sufficiently large and readable on different devices. Text that is too small or improperly scaled reduces application usability.
items.source:
WORLD WIDE WEB CONSORTIUM (W3C). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG). (WCAG)
Nétek, 2020 (Webová kartografie – kapitola písmo)

items.text: Does the application include basic controls for zooming in and out of the map (e.g. + and − buttons)?
items.explanation: The user should be able to easily change the map scale using standard controls.
items.source:
Nétek, 2020 (Webová kartografie – ovládací prvky)
UCGIS GIS&T Body of Knowledge

items.text: Does the application allow returning to the default map view (e.g. using a 'home' button)?
items.explanation: The function for returning to the default view improves orientation in the application and allows a quick return to the original state.
items.source:
Nétek, 2020 (Webová kartografie – interaktivita a ovládání)
UCGIS GIS&T Body of Knowledge

items.text: Is the selected technology suitable for supporting operational management?
items.explanation: The technology stack must meet the requirements for reliability and speed.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Is the application independent of platform, operating system and browser?
items.explanation: Compatibility across different user environments should be ensured.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 5.2 – Obrazovka a webový prohlížeč jako zobrazovací médium, str. 39–43)

items.text: Does the application run without requiring any installation or plugin?
items.explanation: Barriers to running the application in modern browsers should be minimized.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 7.2 – Programovací jazyky, str. 124–125)

items.text: Is page reload not required after every map movement (data are loaded asynchronously)?
items.explanation: Asynchronous data loading provides a smoother user experience without reloading the whole page.
items.source: Front-End Performance Checklist

items.text: Is the application adapted for mobile devices?
items.explanation: Responsive design should support display on phones and tablets.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Does the application include a clear page title <title> (usually corresponding to the main heading)?
items.explanation: This is important for user orientation in browser tabs and for SEO.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Is the application URL memorable (SEO-friendly)?
items.explanation: A clear address structure makes sharing and discoverability easier.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Is the server or hardware solution stable and sufficiently flexible even under high traffic?
items.explanation: The infrastructure must be able to handle the expected load.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 7.4 – Cloud computing, str. 126–127)

items.text: Can the application be launched in an internet environment?
items.explanation: The application should be available online without being limited to a local network, unless it is intended as an internal application.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Does the code declare <!DOCTYPE html>?
items.explanation: This standard for modern web pages ensures correct rendering.
items.source: WORLD WIDE WEB CONSORTIUM (W3C). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

items.text: Does the application load within 3 seconds after launch?
items.explanation: Loading speed is crucial for maintaining user attention.
items.source: WORLD WIDE WEB CONSORTIUM (W3C). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

items.text: Does the application use UTF-8 encoding?
items.explanation: This ensures correct display of diacritics and special characters.
items.source: WORLD WIDE WEB CONSORTIUM (W3C). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

items.text: Are individual code tags properly closed?
items.explanation: Properly closed tags are a basic prerequisite for valid HTML code.
items.source: WORLD WIDE WEB CONSORTIUM (W3C). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

items.text: Does the application code follow the correct HTML structure (html, head, body)?
items.explanation: This is a basic requirement for HTML document validity.
items.source: WORLD WIDE WEB CONSORTIUM (W3C). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

items.text: Does the code correctly use attributes and elements (href, alt, etc.)?
items.explanation: This ensures link functionality and image accessibility.
items.source: WORLD WIDE WEB CONSORTIUM (W3C). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

items.text: Does the application have valid and correct CSS properties and values?
items.explanation: CSS validity helps ensure a consistent appearance across browsers.
items.source: WORLD WIDE WEB CONSORTIUM (W3C). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

items.text: Is server latency for requests for new data lower than 200 ms?
items.explanation: Low server latency is important for smooth application response when working with dynamic data.
items.source: Front-End Performance Checklist

title: Security
description: Trustworthiness, data origin and legal aspects.

items.text: Is the map content current and trustworthy?
items.explanation: The validity and temporal relevance of the presented information should be ensured.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Does the application include a place for copyright and licence information for data layers and services?
items.explanation: Copyright and data-source terms of use must be respected.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Is the author or imprint of the map application provided?
items.explanation: The operator and creator of the application should be clearly identified.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Is the application protected against simple compromise of trustworthiness and security (e.g. by third-party scripts)?
items.explanation: Protection against common threats and potentially unsafe third-party scripts should be ensured.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Are all parts of the application located under the same URL address?
items.explanation: Environmental consistency helps prevent user confusion.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Does the application avoid redirecting the user without their awareness?
items.explanation: Navigation should be transparent and the user should not be unexpectedly redirected to another website.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Does the application avoid hidden or system scripts that run without the user’s awareness?
items.explanation: The application should not contain hidden, malicious or non-transparent scripts that could endanger the user or data.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020.

items.text: Is the application free of serious typographic and spelling errors?
items.explanation: Correct language increases the professional impression and trustworthiness of the application.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 6.6.3 – Písmo, str. 89–92)

items.text: Are error messages and a 404 (Not Found) page defined?
items.explanation: States where the requested content is not found should be handled.
items.source: WORLD WIDE WEB CONSORTIUM (W3C). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG).

items.text: Does the application comply with legal requirements (does not violate laws, copyright, etc.)?
items.explanation: The application should comply with GDPR, accessibility legislation and other relevant legal requirements.
items.source: NÉTEK, Rostislav. Webová kartografie – specifika tvorby interaktivních map na webu. Olomouc: UPOL, 2020. (Kapitola 8.2 – Autorské právo a licence, str. 135–137)

items.text: Has the application undergone load testing?
items.explanation: The application’s stability should be verified under a high number of simultaneous users.
items.source: Front-End Performance Checklist

items.text: Are the map metadata clearly defined (data origin, date of last update)?
items.explanation: Metadata make it possible to assess the origin, currency and trustworthiness of map content.
items.source: Nétek, Kap. 5.1 / GISTBoK [DM-02]

items.text: Does the map clearly state copyright information and data licences?
items.explanation: Clearly stated copyright and licence information helps users understand the terms of use of both the data and the map itself.
items.source: Kapitola 8.2 – Autorské právo a licence, str. 135
